specification.problem: Given a unitary rep R of a finite group G, find a state |psi> whose translates R(g)|psi> are best distinguishable. Apply this to Group Multiplication for two elements (one query, success 2/|G|, generalizing Deutsch) and to the Hidden Conjugating Element problem (one query, success 1 for suitable groups). The tiny instance is Z_2 Deutsch, with S_3 conjugation as an optional extension.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Scope: (1) the general optimal-state and success-probability formula from rep theory, (2) the Z_2 Deutsch instance as the smallest concrete circuit, (3) the conjugation problem on S_3 (center-free, 6 basis states, 3 qubits) as an optional second instance. Outside scope: a general Fourier-transform circuit for arbitrary G, the optimality proof for 2/|G|, the n-tuple Group Multiplication problem, and the explicit query protocol for general G in group multiplication.

symbols.meaning: unitary representation of G on Hilbert space H
maximally entangled state between V_rho and a multiplicity space of dimension min(d_rho,m_rho)
probability of correctly identifying g from R(g)|psi>

equations.label: Optimal state
equations.description: State maximizing the translate-discrimination success probability. Its norm is 1 only when the weights sum to 1, which holds when R contains every irrep; otherwise normalise the weights.
equations.justification: Recalled from the sketch and from known results on optimal discrimination of group-covariant states. The abstract only says such a state can be found.

equations.label: Optimal success probability
equations.description: Maximum probability of discriminating the |G| translates. It equals 1 when the sum equals |G|.
equations.justification: Recalled from the sketch. The abstract says the state with the highest probability can be found but gives no formula.
assumptions: Uniform prior over g in G

equations.label: Group multiplication success
equations.description: Optimal one-query success probability for the product of two group elements. For Z_2 it is 1, as in Deutsch's algorithm.
equations.abstract_quote: we give an algorithm to find the product of two elements of $G$ with a single quantum query with probability $2/|G|$
equations.justification: Stated directly in the abstract. Optimality is also claimed there.

equations.label: Deutsch instance
equations.latex: O_a|x\rangle=|x+a\bmod 2\rangle,\quad O_a|-\rangle=(-1)^a|-\rangle,\quad H(-1)^{a}|-\rangle\text{ on a control }|+\rangle\to|a\rangle
equations.description: Z_2 case. The query acts on |-> in the target and the phase (-1)^a is kicked back to a |+> control. The Hadamard basis then reads a. For Deutsch, a is the XOR of the oracle's two values (the product a+b), which is the quantity learned in one query. In the simplest group-multiplication form there is a single oracle with hidden a, queried once.
equations.abstract_quote: This generalizes Deutsch’s Algorithm from $\hbox{\bbb Z}_{2}$ to an arbitrary finite group.
equations.justification: Inferred from the claim that the algorithm generalizes Deutsch. The explicit circuit is standard background.
assumptions: Phase-kickback form of the oracle on 1 control and 1 target qubit

equations.label: Conjugation oracle
equations.description: The oracle acts by conjugation. The condition gives perfect discrimination of g, but only modulo the center Z(G), since C_g depends only on gZ(G).
equations.abstract_quote: We show that for many groups, including dihedral and symmetric groups, the unknown element can be determined with probability $1$ using a single quantum query.
equations.justification: Inferred by combining the abstract claim with eq_2. The center caveat is my own addition from the sketch and the structure of the problem.
assumptions: Center-free group such as S_3, or identification of g mod Z(G)

registers.name: query
registers.size: ceil(log2|G|) qubits, 1 for Z_2, 3 for S_3
registers.role: holds the group-labelled state psi; the oracle is applied here

registers.name: control
registers.role: receives the kicked-back phase and is measured

specification.initial_state: All qubits |0>. Group elements are encoded as basis states |index(x)> with the index in little-endian binary, so the register value is bits read as an integer with the last character of the counts key being qubit 0.

steps.description: Classically decompose R into irreps and compute d_rho and m_rho. Build psi from eq_1 using standard gates (e.g. a small rotation and CNOT synthesis, not initialize).
Apply the placeholder oracle exactly once (right-multiplication by the hidden element, or conjugation).

Apply the unitary mapping the translates to orthogonal basis states. For Z_2 this is H, and for general G it is the inverse group Fourier transform together with the basis change that undoes the state preparation.
Measure the register in the computational basis and map the bitstring to a group element, respecting little-endian order.

specification.measurement: Measure the query register (and the control for Z_2) in the computational basis after the inverse rotation. The outcome labels the guessed group element.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Map bitstring to group element index with bits[::-1]. For conjugation, report g modulo the center.
assumptions: Smallest instance chosen: Z_2 Deutsch, with S_3 conjugation as an optional second instance
Oracle is a permutation unitary on a group-labelled register
The G-Fourier transform is built offline for small G from standard gates
Single query to one of the two elements in the group multiplication problem
missing_information: Explicit protocol for the group multiplication query with general G, including how the second element is handled
Explicit circuit for the group Fourier transform for non-abelian G
Whether the 2/|G| strategy uses the regular representation or a different one, since the abstract does not say
